claims.text: Buckingham Palace is the official residence and administrative headquarters of the British monarch in London.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The core of the building was originally a large townhouse constructed in 1703 for the Duke of Buckingham and Normanby.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: King George III acquired the property in 1761 to serve as a private residence for Queen Charlotte, when it became known as The Queen's House.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It was not until the accession of Queen Victoria in June 1837 that Buckingham Palace officially became the principal London residence of the monarch.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The palace features the famous East Front balcony where the royal family traditionally gathers to greet the public during national celebrations.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: During the Second World War, a German bomb completely destroyed the palace chapel.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The King's Gallery was built on the site of the destroyed chapel and opened in 1962 to display art from the Royal Collection.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The massive building contains exactly 775 rooms, which includes 19 state rooms, 92 offices, and 188 staff bedrooms.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The palace is effectively a self-contained village that features its own cinema, swimming pool, doctor's surgery, jeweller's workshop, and post office.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The palace grounds boast the largest private garden in all of London.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: During the summer months, the 19 State Rooms used for official royal entertaining are opened to the public.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The famous Changing of the Guard ceremony takes place right outside the palace.
claims.subject: self
